children: said the Unified Patent Court’s Paris Local Division ruled on Oct. 16 that Angelalign systems incorporating its Torque Ridges feature infringe a European patent covering technology used in Align’s Invisalign clear aligners. The decision is subject to appeal.

For investors, the ruling could help Align defend its competitive position by restricting a rival’s use of the disputed technology in 17 European countries. The financial impact remains uncertain: Align’s announcement did not specify a damages amount or estimate the effect on sales, and it said Angelalign had reported discontinuing Torque Ridges in Europe.

According to Align, the court rejected Angelalign’s challenges to the patent’s validity, ordered the recall and destruction of infringing products, and awarded damages and other relief. The restrictions cover markets including Germany, France, Italy and the Netherlands. Align began infringement proceedings against companies within the Angelalign group in August 2025.

Align said Angelalign had introduced a different feature called Pressure Points and publicly indicated it would comply with the ruling. Align disputed Angelalign’s characterization of the replacement as an upgrade, but has not taken a public position on whether Pressure Points infringes its intellectual property. The announcement did not include a direct response from Angelalign.

The decision adds to patent disputes between the companies across several jurisdictions. Align said a February 2026 preliminary injunction involving its ClinCheck Live Update technology was upheld by the UPC Court of Appeal, while proceedings on the merits continue. In China, Angelalign has appealed an August first-instance judgment finding infringement involving treatment-planning technology and related aligners, according to Align.

A separate U.S. International Trade Commission case concerns five patents asserted by Align against Angelalign. Following a July evidentiary hearing, Align said it expects an initial determination in November 2026.

title: Align Technology says European court finds Angelalign infringed patent
